studies.title: Basophil Activation Testing: From Diagnostic Adjunct to Precision Allergy Management.
studies.authors: Catamerò, Francesco, Han, Jooeun, Karabacak, Deniz Eyice, Hoffmann, Hans Jürgen et al.
studies.abstract: Basophils are rare circulating granulocytes that trigger immediate hypersensitivity reactions through IgE-mediated degranulation and also contribute to innate immunity. The basophil activation test (BAT) is a flow cytometry-based functional assay that quantifies basophil reactivity and sensitivity following allergen stimulation, offering a safe, blood-based alternative to in vivo provocation testing. This review summarizes the immunological basis of the BAT, its technical requirements, and its expanding clinical applications across food, respiratory, drug, and hymenoptera venom allergies, autoimmune chronic spontaneous urticaria, and vaccine hypersensitivity. Beyond diagnosis, the BAT increasingly supports monitoring of allergen immunotherapy and biologic treatments, prediction of reaction severity and treatment response, and personalized management decisions. Its performance varies by allergen and clinical context, and wider adoption is constrained by the absence of standardized protocols, validated cut-offs, and reference materials, as well as by basophil non-releasers and dependence on fresh viable blood. Passive BAT and mast cell activation test formats extend testing to patients in whom the conventional BAT is uninterpretable. Automated, data-driven analysis and machine learning-assisted, label-free platforms offer promising routes toward more objective, scalable interpretation. With continued standardization, harmonization, and prospective validation, the BAT is positioned not only as a diagnostic adjunct but as a platform for precision-based allergy management.

studies.title: Adjunctive oral butyrate supplementation in chronic spontaneous urticaria: A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial.
studies.journal: Asian Pacific journal of allergy and immunology
studies.authors: Chiamruchikun, Patcharat, Mitthamsiri, Wat, Sangasapaviliya, Atik, Jaisupa, Nattapon et al.
studies.abstract: Chronic spontaneous urticaria (CSU) is a chronic inflammatory and mast-cell driven skin disease. Butyrate has been extensively studied for its anti-inflammatory effects and its ability to inhibit mast cell activation. To evaluate the efficacy of butyrate supplements as an adjunctive treatment to improve CSU control. Adult patients with CSU were enrolled and randomly assigned to receive 2,400 mg of butyrate or placebo. Both groups received 40 mg/day of bilastine for 4 weeks. The Urticaria Activity Score (UAS7) and Dermatology Life Quality Index (DLQI) were measured at baseline and after 4 weeks. Peripheral blood was analyzed for dysfunctional CRTH2+ regulatory T cells (Tregs) and basophil activation test by flow cytometry method. Of 29 patients, 15 patients in the butyrate group and 14 patients in the placebo group completed the study. After 4 weeks, no significant differences in UAS7, DLQI, CRP, or D-dimer levels between the two groups were observed. Next, we conducted the subgroup analysis of patients with moderate-to-severe CSU (UAS7 ≥ 16). Patients in the butyrate group showed significant improvement in UAS7 (p = 0.003) and DLQI (p = 0.02) compared to the placebo group. The frequency of CRTH2+ Tregs and basophil activation markers also significantly decreased in the butyrate group compared to the placebo group. Adjunctive oral butyrate supplementation was safe but did not significantly improve the prespecified primary outcomes in the overall CSU population. Post-hoc exploratory findings suggested potential clinical and immunological benefits in moderate-to-severe CSU, warranting confirmation in adequately powered randomized trials.

studies.title: 4-O-(E)-Feruloyl-N-feruloyloctopamine suppresses mast cell-mediated allergic airway inflammation and pulmonary fibrosis.
studies.authors: Kim, Yeon-Yong, Jeong, Seungwon, Jang, Hyun-Jae, Lee, Seung Woong et al.
studies.abstract: Previous studies demonstrated that ferulic acid exerts therapeutic effects on various inflammatory disorders, including arthritis, acute respiratory distress syndrome, and asthma. We synthesized a novel ferulic acid derivative (4-O-(E)-feruloyl-N-feruloyloctopamine, FOA), which has not been analyzed previously. We validated whether FOA modulates airway inflammation and fibrosis and unraveled its possible underlying mechanisms. In a murine model of ovalbumin (OVA)-induced airway inflammation, FOA treatment alleviated immune cell recruitment and reduced pro-inflammatory mediator and immunoglobulin (Ig) levels in bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF) and serum, respectively. In BALF and Lung tissue, pro-inflammatory cytokines were significantly suppressed by FOA treatment. FOA administration decreased the recruitment of mast cells into lung tissue and activation. We focused on FOA efficacy using mast cells, which are involved in asthma development. In RBL (rat basophilic leukemia)-2H3 and rat peritoneal mast cells (RPMCs), FOA pretreatment inhibited mast cell degranulation and pro-inflammatory cytokine production through intracellular signaling pathways, including Lyn, Syk, Akt, phosphoinositide 3-kinase, phospholipase Cγ, nuclear factor-κB, and MAPKs. To determine the pro-fibrotic function of activated mast cells, we stimulated mast cells for transforming growth factor-β expression and secretion, contributing to fibrotic symptoms in lung tissues. FOA administration suppressed these fibrotic symptoms. FOA pretreatment exerted anti-fibrotic effects in human lung epithelial cell lines (A549 and NCI-H358) through the suppression of fibrotic factor expression, and in a murine model of bleomycin-induced pulmonary fibrosis. Collectively, our findings suggest that FOA may serve as a promising therapeutic candidate for allergic airway inflammation and pulmonary fibrosis.

studies.title: Serum Vitamin D Levels and Antihistamine Treatment Response in Chronic Spontaneous Urticaria: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
studies.journal: International archives of allergy and immunology
studies.authors: Okumus Guclu, Aysu, Seren, Orbay Tutku, Ozaydn Unal, Sultan, Karatas, Hakan Ömer et al.
studies.abstract: Chronic spontaneous urticaria (CSU) is often refractory, and some patients do not achieve control with second-generation H1-antihistamines (sgAHs). Vitamin D has immunomodulatory effects relevant to mast cell biology, but its relationship with sgAH treatment response, as distinct from disease presence or severity, is poorly characterized. We investigated the association between serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D [25(OH)D] levels and sgAH response in CSU. This retrospective cohort study included patients with active CSU who had a 25(OH)D measurement within the 3 months preceding diagnosis or on the day of diagnosis. Patients who received vitamin D therapy within 6 months before diagnosis or during follow-up, and those with hepatic, renal or systemic autoimmune disease or prior glucocorticoid or immunosuppressant use, were excluded. Treatment response was assessed with the Urticaria Control Test (UCT) after at least 4 weeks on a stable regimen. Patients reaching UCT ≥12 on sgAH monotherapy, at the licensed dose or after updosing, were classified as sgAH-responsive; those with UCT <12 after at least 4 weeks at four-fold dosing were classified as sgAH-refractory. Analyses included univariate comparisons, receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis and age-and sex-adjusted logistic regression. Of 167 patients, 93 (55.7%) were sgAH-responsive and 74 (44.3%) were sgAH-refractory. Median 25(OH)D was higher in sgAH-responsive patients (25.6 vs 15.3 ng/mL; p<0.001). The area under the ROC curve was 0.769 (95% CI 0.693-0.835), and a cutoff of 21.2 ng/mL yielded 67.7% sensitivity and 79.7% specificity. In an age-and sex-adjusted model, each 1 ng/mL increase in 25(OH)D was associated with 12.4% higher odds of sgAH response (OR 1.124, 95% CI 1.075-1.174; p<0.001), independent of season of measurement. Eosinophil and basophil counts, ESR, CRP, thyroid autoantibodies, TSH, total IgE, ANA positivity and comorbidities did not differ between groups. Lower serum 25(OH)D was independently associated with sgAH refractoriness in CSU. Prospective studies are needed to determine whether this reflects a modifiable contributor to treatment response; if confirmed, vitamin D status could be a practical parameter to consider in patients with inadequate response to antihistamines.

To investigate whether preventive oral administration of KQS1 attenuates food-allergy-associated responses and its mechanism. An OVA-induced murine food-allergy model was established with preventive oral gavage of KQS1. Systemic and intestinal allergic-associated outcomes and mast-cell activation were assessed. Primary mouse bone-marrow-derived mast cells and human cord-blood-derived mast cells were used for cellular and mechanistic studies. Pharmacological inhibition of EZH2 and genetic perturbation of KDM6B were used to examine the functional contribution of H3K27me3-related regulation. studies.title: Laryngeal involvement in chronic spontaneous urticaria-associated angioedema: Is there a genuine risk?
studies.authors: Valerieva, Anna, Perego, Francesca, Stancheva, Irena, Petkova, Elena et al.
studies.abstract: Chronic spontaneous urticaria (CSU) affects up to 1% of the population, and 40% of patients develop concomitant angioedema (CSU-AE). While clinically significant laryngeal involvement in mast cell-mediated CSU-AE is considered rare, and large cohorts report no fatal airway compromise, patients frequently present to emergency departments with symptoms perceived as potentially airway affecting. To describe retrospective clinical observations of CSU-AE patients presenting with symptoms suggestive of upper airway involvement and to contextualize these findings within the existing literature. We performed a retrospective descriptive review of consecutive CSU patients evaluated between October 2017 and July 2018 at two tertiary referral centers (Milan, Italy and Sofia, Bulgaria). Medical records were screened for angioedema localization, history of physician-documented laryngeal involvement during emergency evaluations, history of airway interventions, medication exposure, and acute treatment response. Among 1,098 patients, 530 (48%) experienced angioedema and wheals in the context of CSU-AE. Thirteen patients (2%) had objectively documented laryngeal involvement prompting emergency assessment; three patients (all female) underwent endotracheal intubation. No fatalities or loss of consciousness occurred. None had concurrent wheals during the reported laryngeal episodes. History of NSAID exposure preceded some laryngeal exacerbations, though not in intubated cases. None of the patients was receiving ACE inhibitor treatment, all had normal C1 inhibitor (antigen and function) and normal C4. Laryngeal symptoms resolved within hours following standard acute therapy with corticosteroids and/or antihistamines (AHs). Due to the retrospective design, diagnostic work-up for alternative angioedema mechanisms (genetic testing) was incomplete. These observations do not indicate an increased intrinsic airway risk in CSU-AE. Rather, they illustrate diagnostic and management challenges in emergency settings and highlight the importance of mechanism-aware clinical assessment to avoid unnecessary invasive airway interventions. Laryngeal angioedema in CSU-AE is rare and presents with a mild clinical phenotype that does not typically require airway intervention.

studies.title: ROS-Responsive Diselenide-Bridged Dendritic Mesoporous Silica Nanoparticles Enhance Licochalcone D Delivery for Atopic Dermatitis Therapy Associated with Oxidative Stress Modulation and JAK2/STAT5 Inhibition.
studies.authors: Liu, Hua, Ma, Qingsong, Fan, Huiping, Zhang, Dong et al.
studies.abstract: Atopic dermatitis (AD) involves type 2 inflammation, oxidative stress, and aberrant JAK/STAT signaling. Although localized JAK modulation is attractive, delivery remains challenging. Licochalcone D (LCD) has antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties, but poor solubility, limited bioavailability, and dose-dependent cytotoxicity restrict its application. We developed reactive oxygen species (ROS)-responsive diselenide-bridged dendritic mesoporous silica nanoparticles for localized LCD delivery. Public AD transcriptomic datasets and human skin samples were analyzed for oxidative stress and JAK2/STAT5 activation. LCD-loaded nanoparticles ( AD lesions showed enrichment of oxidative stress and JAK/STAT-related pathways, increased ROS, and elevated JAK2/STAT5 phosphorylation.

studies.title: Recurrent mitotic error and purifying selection shape chromosomal mosaicism across human tissues.
studies.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
studies.authors: Tang, David, Kamitaki, Nolan, Si, Yichen, Sexton, Corinne E et al.
studies.abstract: Mosaic chromosomal alterations (mCAs) have been extensively studied in cancer and clonal hematopoiesis but less so in healthy solid tissues. Here, we characterized mCAs in 19 tissues across 25 donors (aged 42-89+ years) by analyzing >200x whole-genome sequencing data generated by the Somatic Mosaicism across Human Tissues (SMaHT) Network. Across 722 tissue samples, we identified 1,008 autosomal mCAs >1 Mb in length and ubiquitous losses of sex chromosomes. Surprisingly, the highest levels of Y chromosome loss in males (5-10% cell fraction in elderly donors) were observed in the lung, adrenal gland, and heart. These tissues also tended to experience more X loss in females, revealing a gradient of mitotic error burden across human tissues. Autosomal aneuploidies displayed distinct tissue-specific patterns indicative of negative selection against most events, except in the adrenal gland, in which low-level aneuploidy was pervasive. In contrast to the adrenal gland, testis rarely harbored aneuploidies but frequently experienced low-level copy-neutral loss of heterozygosity (CN-LOH), suggesting increased mitotic recombination in spermatogonial stem cells. Recurrent X chromosome losses within tissues of female donors exhibited allelic skews explained by a combination of genetic and epigenetic effects. Together, these results show that the chromosomal landscape of aging human tissues is shaped by genetics and recurrent mutations, most but not all of which are held in check by purifying selection.

studies.title: Garlic-derived S-allyl-L-cysteine ameliorates colon-spleen axis pathology in acute colitis.
studies.journal: Phytomedicine : international journal of phytotherapy and phytopharmacology
studies.authors: Han, Deping, Liang, Ruijuan, Zhu, Fengxia, Guan, Xuke et al.
studies.abstract: S-allyl-L-cysteine (SAC), a bioactive organosulfur compound derived from aged garlic, exhibits anti-inflammatory properties, yet its cellular targets and systemic mechanisms in ulcerative colitis (UC) remain undefined. This study aimed to investigate whether SAC confers protection against dextran sulfate sodium (DSS)-induced colitis and to elucidate its mechanism of action, with a particular focus on the colon-spleen axis and neuro-immune crosstalk. Acute colitis was induced in wild-type and CCL7 knockout mice using 2.5% DSS, followed by daily oral SAC administration (3 mg/kg). Disease severity was assessed through clinical parameters, histopathology, and immunohistochemistry. Xenium spatial transcriptomics was employed to map cellular dynamics and intercellular communication. In vitro assays using HCT116 epithelial cells, P815 mast cells, RAW264.7 macrophages, HL-60 neutrophils, and THP-1 monocytes were performed to dissect the underlying molecular mechanisms. SAC treatment significantly alleviated colitis symptoms, reduced mortality, preserved mucosal integrity, and decreased inflammatory cell infiltration. Spatial transcriptomics revealed that injured epithelial cells released TNF-α, which activated subepithelial mast cells via NFκB2 nuclear translocation to produce CCL7. SAC was preferentially and efficiently internalized by mast cells, not macrophages, to suppress this TNF-α/NFκB2/CCL7 signaling pathway. This inhibition abrogated splenic myeloid recruitment through CCR1/2 and CXCR2, supporting a colon-spleen axis that orchestrates systemic inflammation. SAC also redirected neuronal transcription toward repair-oriented pathways and upregulated FTH1, redistributing iron from pro-inflammatory macrophages to epithelial cells. CCL7 deficiency phenocopied SAC's protective effects, with attenuated neuronal-adjacent neutrophilia and preserved mucosal integrity. We unveil an epithelial-TNF-α-mast cell-CCL7-spleen-neuronal injury axis as a key contribution of colitis propagation and suggest SAC as a dietary agent that concurrently curbs systemic myeloid recruitment and relieves enteric neuronal inflammation, thereby attenuating colitis-associated abdominal pain.

studies.title: Baseline immune profiles are associated with positive outcomes in young children with a peanut allergy, enrolled in a randomised clinical trial for oral immunotherapy.
studies.journal: Allergy, asthma, and clinical immunology : official journal of the Canadian Society of Allergy and Clinical Immunology
studies.authors: Coenen, Isabelle, Figliomeni, Abbey, Parkin, Kimberley, de Asis, Judy et al.
studies.abstract: Peanut allergy affects around 3% of Australian infants, can cause life-threatening anaphylactic reactions and often persists throughout life. Oral immunotherapy (OIT) is a promising treatment to achieve desensitisation, but treatment outcomes vary. This study describes the immunological profiles associated with favourable OIT outcomes. This study assessed blood samples from 49 peanut-allergic children (1-4 years old) who participated in the Early Peanut Immunotherapy in Children (EPIC) randomised controlled trial. Children randomised to undergo peanut OIT (n = 24), or to follow the current recommended clinical practise of strict peanut avoidance (n = 25) for twelve months, were immunologically evaluated. Desensitisation outcomes were assessed using an end of treatment (EOT) oral food challenge, and blood samples were collected at baseline, 12-week follow-up (OIT only), and EOT. Thirty immune cell subsets were identified using an established immune cell flow cytometry panel and an FcεR1 expression panel. As part of the clinical trial, OIT induced either partial or complete desensitisation in 91.3% of participants in the intervention group, compared to 20.8% in the avoidance group. After 12 weeks of treatment, OIT-treated patients displayed an expansion of basophils, monocytes and dendritic cells compared to levels at recruitment. At EOT, OIT increased the abundance of CD4 Our findings suggest that immune signatures vary according to OIT clinical response and may have utility in monitoring treatment progress and in identifying children most likely to benefit from OIT in the future.

studies.title: Chemotherapy-induced mast-cell degranulation constrains tertiary lymphoid maturation in lung cancer brain metastasis.
studies.authors: Fu, Minjie, You, Muyuan, Ao, Yongqiang, Zeng, Guichang et al.
studies.abstract: Tertiary lymphoid structures (TLSs) support local adaptive immunity and are associated with favorable antitumor responses across multiple cancers. However, how anticancer treatment reshapes TLS maturation, particularly in lung cancer brain metastasis (LCBM), remains poorly understood. We integrated clinicopathological profiling of LCBM cohorts with bulk and single-cell RNA sequencing, spatial profiling, immune-repertoire analysis, histological validation, and murine intracranial tumor models. Associations between prior treatment and TLS maturation were evaluated using multivariable analyses. Mechanistic studies examined chemotherapy-associated IL-33 release, mast-cell activation, and the effects of PGD2 on antigen-specific T-cell cytotoxicity and B-cell differentiation. Pharmacological inhibition of H-PGDS and mast-cell stabilization were further evaluated in vivo. Mature TLSs were associated with favorable survival in patients with LCBM, whereas preoperative chemotherapy was independently associated with impaired TLS maturation after adjustment for measured clinical and treatment covariates. Consistent with this observation, chemotherapy-treated tumors exhibited increased IL-33 levels, mast-cell accumulation, and enhanced mast-cell degranulation, with spatial analyses placing activated mast cells within TLS-associated immune niches. Mechanistically, IL-33 activated ST2-expressing mast cells, induced NF-κB-associated transcriptional programs. Functionally, mast cell-derived PGD2 suppressed antigen-specific CD8⁺ T-cell cytotoxicity and impaired plasma-cell differentiation, providing a potential link between chemotherapy and weakened local adaptive immunity. In vivo, pharmacological inhibition of H-PGDS enhanced chemotherapy efficacy, while mast-cell stabilization with cromolyn sodium reduced chemotherapy-associated degranulation, increased local adaptive immune-cell infiltration, improved intracranial tumor control, and prolonged survival when combined with chemotherapy. Our findings support a model in which chemotherapy-associated tissue stress activates an IL-33-responsive mast-cell program and restrains TLS-associated adaptive immunity in LCBM. Although this pathway is unlikely to operate as an exclusively linear or mast-cell-specific mechanism, targeting mast-cell-associated inflammatory signaling may provide a strategy to preserve antitumor immunity and improve the therapeutic efficacy of chemotherapy in brain metastasis.

These effects correlate with elevated type-2 cytokines, including interleukin (IL)-3, IL-4, and IL-10. We previously demonstrated that basophils regulate MC activation and protect intestinal barrier integrity during malaria. studies.title: Allergen-IgE Affinity Regulates FcεRI Cluster Internalization and Induces Effective FcεRI Desensitization in Mast Cells.
studies.authors: Nagata, Yuka, Kimura, Miyu, Urayama, Mutsumi, Furukawa, Atsushi et al.
studies.abstract: The immunoglobulin E (IgE) receptor FcεRI undergoes dynamic changes in response to allergens (i.e., Ags; antigens) and IgE properties. Mast cell (MC) responses to high-affinity (dinitrophenyl [DNP]-Fab) and low-affinity (nitrophenyl [2NP]-Fab) Ags demonstrated that affinity differences between Ag and IgE determine subsequent cellular reactions. This study assessed Ag-IgE affinity effect on Ag-induced FcεRI desensitization efficacy and safety. Murine bone marrow-derived MCs (BMMCs) were sensitized using anti-DNP IgE, treated with increasing DNP-Ag and 2NP-Ag concentrations, and subsequently challenged with optimal DNP-Ag concentration. We observed that 2NP-Ag induced FcεRI internalization without MC activation. Both Ags can desensitize FcεRI in BMMCs, with DNP-Ag activating MCs during desensitization, whereas 2NP-Ag achieved FcεRI desensitization without MC activation. IgE-FcεRI cluster response to foreign Ags initiates MC outcomes. The formation of small IgE-FcεRI clusters is crucial for gradual and silent FcεRI internalization. In this study, low-affinity Ag-IgE stimulation forms small IgE-FcεRI clusters, contributing to effective FcεRI desensitization. These results indicate that Ag-IgE affinity is essential for FcεRI desensitization safety.

studies.title: Germination-Assisted LAB-Fermented Soy Protein Gel Matrices with Reduced Sensitizing Potential: Associations with Epitope Disruption, Epithelial Transport, and Mucosal Immune-Cell/Cytokine Shifts.
studies.journal: Journal of agricultural and food chemistry
studies.authors: Wang, Yaqiong, Wang, Yi, Yao, Zhijie, Rui, Xin et al.
studies.abstract: Food allergenicity reflects gastrointestinal bioaccessibility, epithelial transport, and immune recognition rather than intrinsic protein properties alone. Using germination-assisted lactic acid fermentation to engineer soy protein matrices with distinct microstructures, we systematically examined allergen fate across digestion, epithelial transport, and immune responses. Germination-induced remodeling produced looser, more porous gel networks, enhancing gastrointestinal disintegration and proteolytic accessibility. Digestion of remodeled matrices yielded greater loss of epitope-containing peptides, fewer high-molecular-weight immunoreactive fragments, and reduced IgE binding. Multiscale epitope mapping showed fewer digestion-resistant epitope peptides and limited retention of immunoreactive regions. Remodeled matrices enhanced transepithelial peptide transport while lowering the immunoreactivity of transported fractions, indicating altered biological properties rather than reduced transport. In a mouse sensitization model with identical challenge, engineered matrices alleviated allergic responses, suppressing Th2 markers, mast cell activation, and improving barrier and mucosal immune profiles, supporting a multiscale framework for hypoallergenic food design.

studies.title: The CD1d-iNKT Axis Modulates Allergic Responses to Alpha-Gal.
studies.journal: Clinical and experimental allergy : journal of the British Society for Allergy and Clinical Immunology
studies.authors: Wang, Yinghui, Rival, Claudia M, Zhang, Yugen, Vasan, Soorya et al.
studies.abstract: Amblyomma americanum (Aa or lone star tick) bites can induce alpha-gal syndrome (AGS)-allergic responses to mammal products linked to galactose-alpha-1,3-galactose (alpha-gal or α-Gal)-specific (s)IgE. Peripheral blood mononuclear cells in AGS show increased CD4 We injected α-Gal-deficient (AGKO) mice on a C57BL/6J background with: (1) protein-rich Aa tick whole body extracts with or without anti-CD1d monoclonal antibody 19G11; (2) iNKT lipid activator α-galactosylceramide plus α-Gal glycoprotein (cetuximab) or (3) lipid-enriched Aa tick whole body extracts. We profiled circulating CD4 Tick extract injections induced α-Gal sIgG1, expanded circulating Th2 cells, promoted systemic type 2 (T2)-skewed cytokine responses, and primed for dietary alpha-gal-induced mast cell activation in AGKO mice. Activating iNKT cells with alpha-galactosylceramide concurrent with cutaneous α-Gal-glycoprotein injections, or with lipid-enriched tick extracts alone, induced α-Gal-sIgE. Disrupting CD1d-iNKT cell interactions blunted T2 cytokine-producing iNKT cell expansion induced by tick lipids; α-Gal-sIgE production; and α-Gal-induced mast cell activation. Importantly, infesting with adult Aa ticks increased circulating activated iNKT and Th2 cell frequencies and systemic IL-4, α-Gal sIgG1, and sIgE levels, priming mast cells for degranulation after dietary α-Gal challenge. CD1d-iNKT cell interactions may enhance early T2 cytokine production induced by tick bite, supporting α-Gal sIgE production and amplifying α-gal-induced mast cell degranulation primed by tick-induced, systemic T2-skewing.

studies.title: Expression of endoglin (CD105) and its correlation with mast cells across different grades of oral epithelial dysplasia and oral squamous cell carcinoma: A retrospective comparative study.
studies.journal: Journal of oral and maxillofacial pathology : JOMFP
studies.authors: Sharma, Deep, Ojha, Anuradha, George, Jiji, Singh, Ankita et al.
studies.abstract: Oral epithelial dysplasia (OED) represents a histopathological spectrum of oral potentially malignant disorders that may progress to oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC). Angiogenesis plays a pivotal role in tumour initiation, progression, and metastasis. Endoglin (CD105) is a specific marker of neoangiogenesis, while mast cells are known to influence angiogenesis through the release of pro-angiogenic mediators. Evaluating CD105-based microvessel density (MVD) and toluidine blue-stained mast cell density (MCD) may provide valuable insight into the biological behaviour of dysplastic and malignant oral lesions. To assess and compare endoglin (CD105) expression and mast cell density across different grades of oral epithelial dysplasia and oral squamous cell carcinoma, and to evaluate their correlation with disease progression. Histopathologically confirmed cases of oral epithelial dysplasia (mild, moderate, and severe) and oral squamous cell carcinoma (well, moderately, and poorly differentiated) were included. Pyogenic granuloma served as the control group. Immunohistochemical staining for endoglin (CD105) was performed to evaluate mean vascular density, and mast cells were identified using toluidine blue stain. Quantification was carried out in selected hotspot areas under high-power magnification. Data were analysed using appropriate statistical tests. A A progressive increase in Endoglin-positive microvessel density was observed from dysplasia to carcinoma, with the highest values in poorly differentiated OSCC. Mast cell density showed an increase in dysplastic lesions but demonstrated a variable trend with advancing carcinoma grades. Angiogenesis, as assessed by endoglin (CD105), increases significantly with disease progression from dysplasia to carcinoma. Mast cells may play a modulatory role in early angiogenesis, though their role in advanced malignancy remains controversial.

studies.title: PVN CRF/CRF-R1 signaling links stress to bowel dysfunction, anxiety-like behavior, and colonic barrier injury and is modulated by electroacupuncture in IBS-D-like mice.
studies.authors: Huang, Shun, Shen, Chuqiao, Xu, Chen, Wang, Xiyang et al.
studies.abstract: Diarrhea-predominant irritable bowel syndrome (IBS-D) is frequently accompanied by anxiety and intestinal barrier dysfunction, yet the central mechanisms linking stress-related neural signaling to peripheral colonic injury -30y remain incompletely understood. To investigate whether paraventricular hypothalamic nucleus (PVN) CRF/CRF-R1 signaling acts upstream of colonic barrier dysfunction and whether electroacupuncture (EA) alleviates IBS-D-like and anxiety-like phenotypes by modulating this pathway. An IBS-D-like mouse model with anxiety-like behaviors was established by combining chronic restraint stress with intermittent chemical stimulation. Visceral sensitivity, bowel dysfunction, and anxiety-like behaviors were assessed. PVN CRF signaling was bidirectionally manipulated by stereotactic microinjection, and downstream changes in colonic CRF/CRF-R1 signaling, mast cell activation, inflammatory signaling, tight junction-related proteins, and permeability-associated markers were evaluated. Model mice exhibited visceral hypersensitivity, diarrhea-like symptoms, anxiety-like behaviors, and colonic barrier impairment. EA improved both gastrointestinal and affective abnormalities and reduced PVN CRF/CRF-R1 overactivation. Intra-PVN CRF administration reproduced key bowel and behavioral abnormalities in otherwise normal mice, whereas CRF-R1 blockade alleviated these changes in model mice. Central manipulation of PVN CRF signaling was accompanied by corresponding alterations in colonic CRF/CRF-R1 expression, mast cell degranulation, TNF-α/NF-κB/MLCK signaling, tight junction-related proteins, and permeability-associated changes. These findings support a PVN-driven brain-gut-barrier mechanism in which CRF/CRF-R1 signaling contributes to bowel dysfunction, anxiety-like behavior, and colonic barrier injury in IBS-D-like mice. EA alleviated these abnormalities, at least in part, through modulation of this pathway.

studies.title: [Mechanisms of Rosa roxburghii extract on atopic dermatitis in mice based on metabolomics and network pharmacology].
studies.journal: Zhongguo Zhong yao za zhi = Zhongguo zhongyao zazhi = China journal of Chinese materia medica
studies.authors: Ye, Chen-Jie, Lu, Tao, Fang, Li, Tao, Yin-Quan et al.
studies.abstract: To investigate the ameliorative effects and underlying molecular mechanisms of Rosa roxburghii extract(RRT) on 2,4-dinitrochlorobenzene(DNCB)-induced atopic dermatitis(AD) in mice, and to provide a scientific basis for the high-value utilization of R. roxburghii resources, this study prepared RRT using a water extraction method and identified its chemical constituents by UHPLC-Q-Exactive Orbitrap-MS. The therapeutic effects of RRT on AD-related skin lesions were comprehensively evaluated using EASI scoring, hematoxylin-eosin(HE) staining, and toluidine blue(TB) staining. Serum and skin levels of inflammatory cytokines and immunoglobulin E(IgE) were quantified using commercial kits, while Western blot(WB) analysis was used to detect the expression of skin barrier-related proteins, including claudin-1, filaggrin(FLG), and loricrin(LOR). Furthermore, metabolomics combined with network pharmacology was employed to identify core anti-AD pathways and targets of RRT, which were subsequently validated by molecular docking and WB to confirm the regulatory effects on pathway-related proteins. The results showed that 44 bioactive components were identified in RRT. RRT administration dose-dependently reduced the EASI score in AD mice. HE staining demonstrated that RRT effectively alleviated epidermal hyperplasia, abnormal keratinization, and inflammatory cell infiltration, while TB staining indicated a significant reduction in mast cell number and degranulation in skin tissue. Biochemical assays confirmed that RRT significantly downregulated the abnormal expression of interleukin(IL)-6, IL-1β, tumor necrosis factor-α(TNF-α), IL-4, IL-13, and IgE in serum and skin tissues, thereby effectively inhibiting excessive inflammatory responses and immune dysregulation. Meanwhile, RRT remarkably upregulated the expression of claudin-1, FLG, and LOR, contributing to the repair of the impaired skin barrier in AD mice. Metabolomic analysis revealed that RRT reversed abnormal levels of multiple differential metabolites in serum and skin, with the arachidonic acid(AA) metabolic pathway identified as the core regulatory pathway. Integrated network pharmacology analysis further confirmed that this pathway plays a key role in the anti-AD effects of RRT and identified related core targets. Molecular docking demonstrated that multiple active components of RRT exhibited strong binding affinities with key proteins in the AA metabolic pathway. WB and kit-based assays showed that RRT significantly inhibited the expression of key enzymes in this pathway, including phospholipase A2 group ⅣA(PLA2G4A), cyclooxygenase-1(COX-1), and arachidonate 5-lipoxygenase(ALOX-5), as well as downstream metabolites such as AA, prostaglandin E2(PGE2), and leukotriene B4(LTB4). In conclusion, RRT may alleviate AD symptoms in mice through the synergistic regulation of the AA metabolic pathway mediated by multiple bioactive components.

studies.title: Inner-Surface Charge Mapping in Confined Systems via Electrical Double-Layer Dynamics.
studies.authors: Gao, Jianyuan, Feng, Yiwen, Zhu, Yufeng, Ma, Hongyang et al.
studies.abstract: Surface charges at solid-liquid interfaces govern diverse emerging interfacial phenomena, yet their quantification in confined geometries remains challenging. Here, we report an electrical double-layer dynamics-enabled method for inner-surface charge characterization (EISC), using water as a mobile and conformal probe. Unlike conventional techniques that require access to exposed surfaces, the EISC method converts charge transfer at water-solid interfaces into measurable, spatially resolved electrical signals, enabling reconstruction of local surface charge density along otherwise inaccessible inner surfaces. Quantitative validation using a roll-up platform, where predefined surface charges are introduced via electrowetting, shows strong agreement with electrostatic voltmeter measurements and enables quantitative reconstruction of diverse charge distributions. Leveraging this capability, we investigate water-solid contact electrification in tubular channels and reveal a velocity-dependent charge separation process at the receding contact line, with grounding effects pronounced at low velocities. Furthermore, direct mapping of charge evolution in droplet electricity generators demonstrates that device performance is governed not only by droplet-carried charges but also by interfacial charge accumulation and redistribution on the solid surface. This work establishes a versatile strategy for probing interfacial charges in confined systems and provides valuable mechanistic insights into charge transfer processes at water-solid interfaces.

Herein, we report the discovery of a pyrazolopyrimidine series as potent and orally bioavailable MRGPRX2 antagonists. studies.title: Immune heterogeneity and the immune-barrier-hydrops framework in Ménière's disease: current evidence, uncertainties, and testable hypotheses.
studies.authors: Guan, Dongmei, Liu, Xinghong, Zhang, Xiaoyi, Zhang, Jingqi et al.
studies.abstract: Ménière's disease presents with episodic vertigo, fluctuating sensorineural hearing loss, tinnitus, and aural fullness, and commonly features endolymphatic hydrops. Yet similar hydropic phenotypes arise in patients with markedly different clinical courses, patterns of bilateral involvement, and treatment responses, suggesting that more than one upstream process may lead to hydrops. Human tissue studies, peripheral immune profiling, allergy- and autoimmunity-associated findings, and blood-labyrinth barrier imaging all point to possible immune contributions in some patients. Their interpretation remains constrained by selected tissue sources, inconsistent definitions of disease stage, heterogeneous assays, and limited independent replication. We examined four candidate effector mechanisms: innate inflammatory amplification and inflammasome signaling; type 2 immunity and mast-cell-mediated modulation of vascular or fluid homeostasis; antibody-, immune-complex-, or complement-mediated injury; and antigen-specific cytotoxic T-cell injury. We distinguished direct observations from the human inner ear from peripheral and imaging associations, experimental perturbations, and mechanistic inference. We then evaluated these evidence streams against four competing causal structures: immune-first, hydrops- or tissue-stress-first, common-upstream-factor, and nonimmune hydropic models. In this framework, the blood-labyrinth barrier is not assumed to be an obligatory step between immune activation and hydrops. Its biological state may instead act as a mediator, effect modifier, common consequence, or component of nonimmune microvascular disease, depending on the causal structure under consideration. MRI enhancement, in turn, remains an imperfect and protocol-dependent proxy for that state. Current evidence does not distinguish these models reliably at the individual-patient level or support stable immune endotypes for treatment selection. It does, however, make two stronger claims difficult to sustain: that MD follows a universal immune-first sequence and that immune activity is required for hydropic progression in every patient. The framework is therefore most useful for separating immune detection, mechanistic contribution, and causal initiation, while specifying which observations would discriminate among competing models. Resolving those models will require longitudinal cohorts that align clinical events with repeated immune and standardized imaging measurements, complemented where feasible by local human samples and pathway-specific perturbation.

studies.title: Discovery of scutellarin as a MRGX2 agonist via MRGX2/CMC strategy and revelation of its pseudo-allergic mechanism.

studies.abstract: Shu-Gan-Ning injection (SGN) is widely used clinically to treat hepatopathy, improve liver function, and enhance immunity. However, pseudo-allergic reactions (PARs) occur after administration and the causative compounds remain unclear. Therefore, it is of paramount importance to pinpoint the "culprit" compound in SGN and explore its underling mechanism. Mas-related G protein-coupled receptor X2 cell membrane chromatography (MRGX2/CMC)-HPLC-MS was established and used to "capture" and identify risk components in SGN. The interactions between risk components and MRGX2 were investigated by integrating MRGX2/CMC detection, virtual docking, and frontal analysis assays. MRGX2-knockdown LAD2 cell models were used to verify the specific target of the risk components and the signaling pathways that trigger PARs. C57BL/6 mice were used to evaluate the PARs induced by hazardous compounds. The conditional knockout mice model was used to evaluate the key role of MAS-related G protein-coupled receptor, member B2 (MRGB2) in mast cells We identified scutellarin, baicalin, and oroxyloside as MRGX2-binding components in SGN. Affinity analysis revealed Collectively, these findings identify scutellarin as an MRGX2 agonist and a pseudo-allergic risk compound in SGN, highlighting the need for quality control measures for scutellarin in baicalin-containing preparations.

studies.abstract: Idiopathic rhinitis (IR) is characterized by nasal hyperreactivity (NHR), which is frequently triggered by temperature variation (TV), as often observed in clinical practice in autumn and winter. While it is generally believed to be associated with TRP channels and neuroimmune pathways, the specific neuroimmune mechanisms underlying TV-induced IR (TV-IR) remain elusive. To elucidate the sensory neuroimmune mechanisms underlying TV-IR. Neuropeptide levels in the nasal mucosa from IR patients and controls were assessed by ELISA. A newly established murine model of TV-IR was created using repeated cold exposure. Wild-type, Trpa1 IR patients exhibited increased substance P (SP) levels in nasal mucosa during winter. TV induced IR in mice, with increased expression of SP and neuromedin B (NMB) in nasal mucosa and trigeminal ganglia. studies.title: Elevated Risk of Psychotropic Drug Prescriptions in Adults With Mastocytosis: A Danish Matched Cohort Study.
studies.authors: Jørgensen, Maren Poulsgaard, Øvlisen, Andreas Kiesbye, Jensen, Jonas Faartoft, Kristensen, Helene Bjørg et al.
studies.abstract: Mastocytosis is a clonal mast cell disorder characterized by chronic mediator-related symptoms and heterogeneous systemic involvement. Neuropsychiatric symptoms are frequently reported, yet population-based evidence on incident depression and/or anxiety remains limited. To examine the mental health burden among patients with mastocytosis. We conducted a population-based matched cohort study using Danish health registers to evaluate incident, pharmacologically treated depression/anxiety among adult patients diagnosed with mastocytosis between 2005 and 2023. Patients were matched 1:5 with individuals from the general Danish population on age, sex, Charlson Comorbidity Index, and educational level. Individuals with psychotropic drug (PD) prescription within 10 years prior to index were excluded. Cumulative risks were estimated using the Aalen-Johansen estimator, and hazard ratios (HRs) were calculated using Cox proportional hazard regression. We included 874 patients with mastocytosis and 4370 comparators. Patients had a higher risk of incident PD prescription in the 10 years following diagnosis (p < 0.001). The 5-year cumulative risk was 13.1% in patients and 8.4% in comparators. The HR for incident PD use was 1.72 (95% confidence interval 1.38-2.15, p < 0.001). Results were consistent across sensitivity and landmark analyses. Higher age, comorbidity, and shorter education were associated with increased risk. Mastocytosis was associated with an increased risk of PD prescriptions, possibly reflecting an increased burden of pharmacologically treated depression and/or anxiety, implying the importance of mental health awareness in clinical management.

Their long-lasting skin complications include dry skin, chronic urticaria, psoriasis, and fibrosis; however, studies on these effects are limited, and a useful

studies.title: IL-17Rb mediates the pathogenesis of allergic rhinitis through STAT6-dependent regulation of TH2 cells and type 2 inflammatory cytokines.
studies.authors: Wei, Meng-Yi, Liu, Zheng, Chen, Qi, Li, Hao et al.
studies.abstract: Allergic rhinitis (AR) is characterized by a T helper 2 (Th2)-cell-mediated immune imbalance, yet its upstream molecular drivers remain poorly defined. Interleukin-17 receptor B (IL-17Rb) has been implicated in type 2 inflammation, but its precise functional role and mechanism in AR pathogenesis are unclear. This study aimed to identify key immunoregulatory genes in AR via bioinformatics and to comprehensively elucidate the functional role and mechanisms of IL-17Rb using both in vivo animal and in vitro cellular models. Candidate genes were screened using GEO datasets and machine learning. An HDM-induced AR murine model and in vitro cell models were utilized. AAV-mediated IL-17Rb knockdown or overexpression, alongside a specific STAT6 inhibitor (AS1517499), were employed. Evaluations included nasal symptoms, histopathology, STAT6 activation, and parameters of Th2 inflammation alongside the Th1/Th17/Treg balance (IL-4/5/13, IFN-γ, IL-17A, IL-10). Bioinformatics identified IL-17Rb as a pivotal upregulated gene in AR, correlating with Th2 infiltration (r = 0.74). In vivo, IL-17Rb knockdown alleviated AR symptoms, eosinophil/mast cell infiltration, and type 2 cytokine release. Importantly, it rectified the AR-associated immune imbalance by restoring IFN-γ (Th1) and IL-10 (Treg) while reducing IL-17A (Th17). Conversely, IL-17Rb overexpression exacerbated Th2 inflammation and STAT6 phosphorylation. Co-administration of AS1517499 successfully abrogated these overexpression-induced effects, confirming a STAT6-dependent mechanism. Furthermore, in vitro blockade of IL-17Rb inhibited IL-25-promoted Th2 differentiation and STAT6 activation. IL-17Rb is a critical upstream immunoregulator in AR, driving STAT6-dependent Th2 inflammation and broadly modulating the Th1/Th17/Treg balance. Targeting the IL-17Rb/STAT6 axis represents a promising therapeutic strategy.

studies.title: A framework for understanding mast cell activation syndrome from a complex adaptive systems perspective.
studies.authors: Van Zyl, Werner Richardt, Henning, Sanchen
studies.abstract: Mast Cell Activation Syndrome (MCAS) challenges conventional reductionist medical models because patients experience fluctuating symptoms across autonomic, immune, gastrointestinal, and behavioural domains, with substantial inter-individual variability and often only partial responses to organ-specific interventions. This conceptual approach reframes MCAS as a complex adaptive system in which chronic illness emerges from interacting feedback dynamics spanning the nervous, immune, behavioural, and environmental domains, rather than from isolated dysfunction within a single subsystem. The framework identifies two primary reinforcing feedback structures: a nervous system loop characterised by autonomic and stress-related dysregulation, and an immune system loop characterised by escalating inflammatory activity. Their persistent coupling generates higher-order emergent dynamics, including amplification, persistence, and instability, which are moderated by balancing regulatory processes that support adaptive stability. This systems perspective addresses fluctuating symptoms, multisystem involvement, and variable treatment responses commonly observed in MCAS. From this perspective, health reflects the capacity to maintain functional adaptation under perturbation, whereas disease emerges when dynamics exceed the system's regulatory capacity. The framework is proposed as a hypothesis-generating scaffold that complements established biomedical approaches and seeks to stimulate future empirical research into the systems-level dynamics of chronic multisystem illness.

studies.title: Comorbidities in Chronic Spontaneous Urticaria: Integrating Disease Drivers and Systemic Consequences.
studies.authors: Kim, Joo-Hee, Kim, Mi-Ae, Ye, Young-Min
studies.abstract: Chronic spontaneous urticaria (CSU) is a mast cell-driven inflammatory skin disorder traditionally considered self-limiting and non-life-threatening. However, accumulating evidence suggests that CSU is associated with multiple comorbidities, reflecting systemic immune and neuroinflammatory dysregulation. These comorbidities may act as both triggers and consequences of disease activity, forming a complex network centered on mast cell activation. Autoimmune diseases, particularly autoimmune thyroid disease, are strongly associated with CSU, especially in the type IIb autoimmune endotype. By contrast, type I autoallergic CSU is associated with immunoglobulin E (IgE) autoantibodies. Atopic diseases, neuroimmune interactions, and psychiatric conditions may further contribute to disease persistence through mechanisms involving IgE signaling and substance P-mediated mast cell activation via Mas-related G protein-coupled receptor X2. Metabolic and cardiovascular comorbidities have also been reported, with recent large-scale cohort studies strengthening the evidence for an association with cardiovascular risk, although causality remains unestablished. Associations with malignancy remain uncertain, whereas recent real-world studies suggest increased mortality among patients with CSU, potentially reflecting the underlying comorbidity burden rather than direct disease effects. Importantly, effective disease control may improve CSU outcomes and associated comorbidities. A comprehensive, mechanism-based approach that integrates comorbidity assessment into clinical management is essential for optimizing patient care.

studies.title: Environmental Ligands of the Aryl Hydrocarbon Receptor in Allergic Rhinitis: Immune and Neuroimmune Mechanisms.
studies.authors: Xiong, Yalan, Han, Jia, Yang, Zhaoxin, Liu, Yongqin et al.
studies.abstract: Allergic rhinitis (AR) is an immunoglobulin E (IgE)-mediated chronic inflammatory disease. Although type 2 immune responses are central to AR, environmental exposures, epithelial barrier dysfunction, and neuroimmune interactions also contribute to disease development. The aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AhR) is a ligand-activated transcription factor that links environmental signals to immune responses. Elevated AhR expression in peripheral blood mononuclear cells from patients with AR has been associated with clinical severity. In non-AR experimental systems, AhR suppresses histamine-associated interleukin-6 (IL-6) production in macrophages, whereas 2,3,7,8-tetrachlorodibenzo-p-dioxin (TCDD) reduces acetylcholinesterase (AChE) expression and activity in neuronal cells. These findings suggest possible links to nasal inflammation and cholinergic regulation, but their contribution to nasal symptoms in AR remains to be established. In addition, AhR modulates mast-cell, B-cell, and T-cell responses in a ligand- and cell-dependent manner. Overall, AhR may exert protective or pathogenic effects depending on the activating ligand and target cell type, suggesting that its therapeutic potential in AR lies in ligand- and cell-specific modulation.

studies.title: Candidate biomarkers predicting clinical outcome after hyperbaric oxygen against chronic radiation cystitis.
studies.authors: Giglio, Daniel, Sallam, Lana, Thorsell, Annika, Mölne, Johan et al.
studies.abstract: Hyperbaric oxygen (HBO2) is effective against radiation cystitis. In this exploratory analysis we employed proteomics to assess biomarkers predicting clinical efficacy and the pharmacodynamics of HBO2 in radiation cystitis. Global quantitative proteomics was performed on biopsies taken before and after HBO2 in patients with radiation cystitis from the RICH-ART trial (NCT01659723). The proteome of HBO2 responders (R) was compared to non-responders (NR) and between R and NR at baseline. Immunohistochemistry was employed to assess the expression of potential biomarkers in urinary bladder biopsies. Biological processes were identified by using the STRING database. Among proteins more expressed in R than NR at baseline were neutrophil defensin 1 and less expressed were chymase and mast cell carboxypeptidase A (CPA3). Among processes differentiating R from NR at baseline were processes regulating translation and complement activation. The top enriched biological processes in NR after HBO2 were processes regulating antigen processing and presentation. Only a few processes were affected by HBO2 in responders. No significant differences in the number of chymase+, CPA3 + and tryptase+ mast cells were observed in bladder specimens between R and NR before and after HBO2. The staining intensity of tryptase, chymase, CPA3 and complement factors C3, C4 and C8 were similar between R and NR and after HBO2. Multiple processes regulating the immune system, complement activation and translation in radiation cystitis are changed after HBO2. However, only a few processes were associated with the clinical efficacy of HBO2. The involvement of mast cells in the pathogenesis of radiation cystitis is suggested.

studies.title: Single-cell RNA sequencing reveals pro-tumorigenic intestinal mast cell programs in colorectal cancer.
studies.authors: Putro, Erisa, Carnevale, Alessia, Marangio, Caterina, Pietropaolo, Giuseppe et al.
studies.abstract: Mast cells (MCs) are multifunctional immune cells with context-dependent functions in cancer. In colorectal cancer (CRC), their contribution remains debated, suggesting that distinct MC subsets may either support tumor progression or promote anti-tumor immunity. Using single-cell RNA sequencing in a mouse model of inflammation-driven CRC, we uncovered extensive MC plasticity during tumor progression. Transcriptomic profiling and pseudotime trajectory analysis revealed a transition from precursor-like MCs exclusively present in adjacent tissue to differentiated tumor-associated MC (TAMC) subsets. TAMCs displayed a distinct repertoire of proteases and pro-inflammatory cytokines, contributing to increased vascular permeability and recruitment of additional immune cells. Moreover, TAMCs exhibited upregulation of molecules with immunosuppressive potential and underwent a tumor microenvironment (TME)-driven metabolic reprogramming. Accordingly, antibody-mediated MC depletion reduced tumor burden. Notably, most of the transcriptional features identified in a murine CRC model were recapitulated in human CRC, supporting the translational relevance of this MC program. Our findings identify a tumor-adapted MC state that orchestrates immune evasion and tissue remodeling during CRC progression, supporting the notion that MC are reprogrammed toward an immune-suppressive and pro-tumorigenic phenotype.

studies.title: Sex differences in the effect of viable cell-containing and heat-killed Roseburia faecis on repeated water avoidance stress-induced irritable bowel syndrome Wistar rat model.
studies.authors: Ha, Sungchan, Kim, Nayoung, Nam, Ryoung Hee, Jin, Isom et al.
studies.abstract: Roseburia faecis has been reported to mitigate irritable bowel syndrome (IBS), which is characterized by altered intestinal motility, mucosal immune activation, and gut microbial dysbiosis. This study aimed to evaluate the sex-dependent effects of heat-killed R. faecis (HK-BBH024) and a viable cell-containing R. faecis preparation (L-BBH024) in a repeated water avoidance stress (rWAS)-induced IBS Wistar rat model. Fecal pellet output (FPO) and colonic mast cell infiltration were measured in the rWAS IBS model induced in 7-week Wistar rats (males and females). Gut microbial composition and function were analyzed by 16S rRNA sequencing and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes pathway prediction, with or without BBH024 treatment. The marked rWAS-induced increase in FPO in both sexes was reduced by HK-BBH024 and L-BBH024. rWAS also increased colonic mast cell infiltration in the proximal colon and the mRNA expression of protease-related genes, whereas L-BBH024 attenuated these sex differences. Specifically, L-BBH024 was associated with a borderline decrease in mast cell infiltration and suppressed Prss1 and Prss2 mRNA expression in females, whereas Prss3 expression was reduced in males. Microbiota profiling showed that rWAS-associated alterations in beta diversity, selected bacterial taxa, linear discriminant analysis-derived microbial biomarkers, and predicted KEGG functional pathways were more evident in females. Both preparations reduced rWAS-induced FPO in both sexes. In the L-BBH024 experiment, additional changes in mast cell infiltration, protease-related gene expression, and microbial features were more evident in females.

studies.title: Gut Bacteriome and Mycobiome Signatures and Differential Allergen-Driven Outcome in Peanut and OVA Anaphylaxis and Their Modulation by Betanin.
studies.authors: Noor, Aziz Ullah, Xu, Yukai, Liu, Zhipeng, Li, Xin et al.
studies.abstract: Food allergy (FA) pathogenesis is closely associated with perturbations of the enteric ecosystem; however, comparative studies examining how distinct allergen triggers differentially affect the enteric mycobiome (total fungal community residing in the gastrointestinal tract) and the enteric bacteriome (total bacterial community residing in the gastrointestinal tract) remain limited. Mapping these allergen-specific patterns of dysbiosis is critical for understanding the pathogenesis and designing targeted therapies. We investigated betanin, a naturally occurring bioactive compound with potent antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties as a prophylactic agent capable of resolving allergen-specific dysbiosis and restoring immune homeostasis and intestinal barrier integrity. We established parallel peanut and ovalbumin (OVA) FA mouse models, administered betanin prophylactically across the sensitization and challenge phases, and evaluated its effects on the allergic outcomes. Efficacy was assessed by measuring anaphylactic symptom scores, allergic biomarkers (total IgE), allergen-specific IgE, histamine, and mast cell protease-1 (mMCPT-1), Th1/Th2 cytokine profiles, and their associated transcription factors (GATA3 and T-bet), intestinal barrier integrity markers, and tight junction protein expression. Allergen-specific microbial shifts were characterized by using ITS2 and 16S rRNA amplicon sequencing. Betanin significantly attenuated the anaphylactic symptoms in both models. It suppressed the Th2-driven allergic cascade, evidenced by GATA3 downregulation and concurrent reductions in IL-4, IL-5, IL-13, allergen-specific IgE, histamine, and mMCPT-1. Betanin intervention notably restored intestinal villus architecture, indicating improved intestinal structural integrity, which was further supported by the upregulated tight junction proteins (i.e., claudin-1, occludin, and tight junction protein 1). Furthermore, betanin restored allergic-associated dysbiosis with both mycobiome and bacteriome enriching

studies.title: A progressive ODE model of seasonal allergic rhinitis: from core Th2 axis to 21-dimensional multi- pathway integration with seasonal dynamics and directional assessment.
studies.authors: Zhang, Qiang, Hu, Houyang, Yue, Yi, Qi, Wenwen et al.
studies.abstract: Seasonal allergic rhinitis (SAR) affects approximately 400 million individuals worldwide, yet a quantitative framework integrating the complete immunological cascade from allergen exposure to clinical symptoms is lacking. Individual pathways (Th2/IgE, TLR4/NF-κB, Th17/Treg) have been characterized in isolation, but their interactions and relative contributions to symptom generation remain poorly understood. We constructed a progressively extended ordinary differential equation (ODE) model evolving from a 10-dimensional core Th2/IgE/mast cell/eosinophil axis to a 21-dimensional system integrating TLR4/MyD88/NF-κB innate immunity and Th17/Treg imbalance with seasonal priming and tolerance dynamics. The model was calibrated against published cytokine data (Leaker 2016, Linton 2025) and validated against clinical trial drug efficacy (Corren 2021, Bauer 2023). Sobol global sensitivity analysis (5,888 samples, 21 parameters) was performed. A 2,000-patient virtual cohort was generated with lognormal parameter distributions (CV = 30%), and PCA-reduced K-means clustering (PC1-PC2 of six output metrics) identified virtual subtypes. Convergence was verified by doubling the base sample size to N = 512: all S1 and ST indices changed by less than 0.013, confirming adequate convergence at the original N = 256. The core model reproduces the biphasic symptom profile (immediate peak 7.0 at 1.9h, late plateau 3.4 at 12-24h) and reveals a mechanistic dichotomy: the immediate peak is governed by the mast cell-mediator axis while total burden is controlled by the eosinophil-resolution axis. The 19-dimensional extension shows that TLR4 and Th17/Treg pathways primarily modulate the late-phase response (11.3% AUC reduction via IL-10 suppression). Sobol analysis identifies the IL-10/Treg axis as the 3rd-4th most important determinant of total symptom burden. The seasonal extension captures immunological priming (IL-5 + 46.1%). Three virtual subtypes map to published AR phenotypes. The model predicts that the Th17/Treg ratio shows a stronger directional association with late-phase severity than IgE, consistent with published clinical data. This progressive ODE model provides a quantitative framework for understanding SAR pathway interactions and generates five testable hypotheses for future experimental validation. The finding that 22% of simulated individuals in the virtual cohort exhibit a severe IL-17-high phenotype supports the hypothesis that Th17/Treg-targeted therapies may benefit a biologically defined subgroup of SAR patients, warranting validation in real patient cohorts.

studies.title: Multi-omics analysis revealed that Jingfang Mixture alleviates inflammation in an OVA/Al(OH)
studies.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
studies.authors: Song, Xiaowen, Liu, Xuexin, Yang, Le, Yan, Guangli et al.
studies.abstract: The systemic and relapsing nature of urticaria cannot be fully explained by cutaneous mast-cell activation alone. Whether the gut contributes, and whether a multi-component formula such as Jingfang Mixture (JF) acts through a gut-skin route, have not been tested together at the level of microbiota, metabolites, and skin signaling together. Using an OVA (ovalbumin)/Al(OH) JF suppressed both Th2 (IgE (immunoglobulin E), IL-4 (interleukin-4)) and Th17/pro-inflammatory (IL-6 (interleukin-6), TNF-α (tumor necrosis factor-α), IL-17 (interleukin-17)) responses, improved intestinal barrier-associated abnormalities, and partially reversed gut dysbiosis by restoring SCFA-producing bacteria ( Collectively, our findings indicate that JF mitigates urticaria-like inflammation, likely through gut microbiota and modulating SCFA, bile acid, tryptophan, and lipid metabolism. This multi-omics evidence suggests that JF may act through the gut microbiota-metabolite-skin signaling axis to confer anti-urticarial benefits. Nevertheless, further causal validation experiments and clinical investigations are warranted.

studies.title: Stem cell therapy attenuates cerebellar histological alterations and blood-brain barrier disruption in experimental fibromyalgia: involvement of mast cells, autophagy, and NLRP3/IL-1β neuroinflammatory pathway.
studies.authors: Mokhemer, Sahar A, Abdelghany, Asmaa K, Hassan, Salma M, AbdelHaleem, Aliaa Hamdy
studies.abstract: Fibromyalgia is a prevalent and debilitating condition that results in generalized musculoskeletal pain, trouble sleeping, exhaustion, psychological challenges, and social problems. As a consequence of fibromyalgia's substantial therapeutic and socioeconomic burden caused by its high prevalence, uncertain etiology, wide spectrum of clinical manifestations, and sophisticated therapy, a considerable interest has emerged in investigating novel aspects of its pathophysiology, particularly those related to anxiety, depression, and cerebellar histological alterations. Such investigations may contribute to the development of effective therapeutic strategies, including the use of bone marrow-derived mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs) as a promising treatment approach. Rats were randomly divided into three groups: control, fibromyalgia and fibromyalgia-stem cell groups. Behavioral assessment was carried out. Cerebellar cortices were collected for histological, immunohistochemical, and morphometric analysis. Fibromyalgia group revealed anxiety-like behavioral changes, and neurodegenerative changes with blood-brain barrier (BBB) affection. Furthermore, NLRP3 and IL-1β immune-expression were significantly increased, with significant increase in the total number of mast cells with marked degranulation. Additionally, there was a significant decrease in Calbindin D-28k (CB), Beclin-1 and LC3 immune-expression. Fibromyalgia-stem cells group revealed amelioration in behavioral alterations, histological improvement, significant decrease in CD117, NLRP3 and IL-1β immune-expression, besides a significant increase in CB, Beclin-1 and LC3 immune-expression. This study represents one of the first experimental studies investigating the potential therapeutic value of BMSCs therapy in fibromyalgia-related cerebellar damage through neuroprotective mechanisms involving enhancement of autophagy, mast cell deactivation, and suppression of NLRP3/IL-1β mediated neuroinflammation with improvement of BBB structural integrity.

studies.title: Surface chemistry governs early redox and cytokine responses to superparamagnetic iron oxide nanoparticles across hepatic-relevant cell models.
studies.authors: Heaton, Bethany J, Sikora, Aneta, Bartczak, Dorota, Goenaga-Infante, Heidi et al.
studies.abstract: Superparamagnetic iron oxide nanoparticles (SPIONs) are increasingly utilised in biomedical and nanomedicine applications, raising important questions regarding early interactions with hepatic cellular systems. This study investigated how surface chemistry influences the biological behaviour of SPIONs across hepatic-relevant cell models through integrated physicochemical characterisation and response screening. Carboxyl (CAR), amine (AMI), and polyethylene glycol (PEG)-coated SPIONs were characterised in biologically relevant media, revealing coating-dependent agglomeration. SPION exposure (2-24 h) was conducted in THP-1 (macrophage-like), Hep G2 (hepatocyte), EA.hy926 (endothelial), and HMC-1.1 (mast cell) models to assess cytotoxicity, redox balance and inflammatory signalling. SPION-induced reactive oxygen species generation and reduced glutathione depletion occurred in a coating- and cell-type-dependent manner, with THP-1 cells showing the greatest sensitivity. Cytokine profiling revealed different responses across models. THP-1 cells demonstrated pronounced pro-inflammatory activation, including increased IL-8, IL-1β and IL-18 secretion, with PEG-SPIONs driving the strongest effects. Conversely, Hep G2 cells exhibited a largely suppressive phenotype characterised by reduced cytokine secretion, while EA.hy926 and HMC-1.1 cells displayed temporally and ligand-dependent responses. Across models, biological responses were associated with nanoparticle dispersion behaviour, supporting agglomeration as an important determinant of early nanoparticle-cell interactions. he association between altered dispersion, redox perturbation and inflammatory responses supports a model in which SPION surface chemistry influences nanoparticle behaviour in biological media, thereby modulating oxidative stress and inflammatory signalling in a cell-dependent manner. Notably, these responses occurred in the absence of overt cytotoxicity, highlighting early perturbations in redox and inflammatory signalling as sensitive indicators of nanoparticle biological activity that may precede overt cellular damage.

studies.title: The potential therapeutic efficacy of platelet-rich plasma gel on experimentally induced localized scleroderma in adult male albino rats.
studies.authors: El-Shafei, Asmaa Ahmed, Hosny, Sara Adel, El Sayed, Hagar, Mohamed, Hala Hassan
studies.abstract: Localized scleroderma, or morphea, is an autoimmune fibrotic disorder characterized by dermal or deeper tissue inflammation and excessive collagen deposition, leading to skin thickening, sclerosis, and eventual atrophy. Early diagnosis is essential to prevent permanent cosmetic and functional impairment. In this condition, COX-2 contributes to early inflammatory signaling through prostaglandin production, which promotes TGF-β1-mediated fibrosis and the differentiation of fibroblasts into α-SMA-positive myofibroblasts. The bleomycin-induced rat model closely reproduces these pathological changes and provides a useful platform for therapeutic evaluation. This study investigated the therapeutic potential of topical platelet-rich plasma (PRP) hydrogel in bleomycin-induced localized scleroderma in adult male albino rats using serological, biochemical, histological, immunohistochemical, ultrastructural, and morphometric analyses. Twenty-four adult male albino rats (200-250 g) were divided into control (saline-injected, n = 6) and experimental LS groups (bleomycin 0.1 mg/0.1 mL SC daily for 4 weeks, n = 18), further subdivided for confirmation, untreated, and PRP-treated (300 μL Carbopol 940-based PRP gel topically twice weekly for weeks 5-8). PRP was prepared from 10 healthy rats' blood via double centrifugation and activated with CaCl2. Assessments included serum biomarkers (ELISA), tissue staining (H&E, Masson's, toluidine blue, IHC), electron microscopy, morphometry (Leica Qwin 500 C), and statistics (ANOVA, p < 0.05 via SPSS 16). Bleomycin induced progressive localized scleroderma-like skin changes characterized by oxidative stress, collagen deposition, mast cell infiltration, and increased expression of COX-2, TGF-β1, and α-SMA. PRP hydrogel treatment significantly improved these alterations, with restoration toward control values in biochemical markers and partial recovery of skin architecture. PRP hydrogel exerts promising antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and antifibrotic effects in bleomycin-induced localized scleroderma, suggesting its potential as a local therapeutic approach for morphea.

studies.title: Whey protein hydrolysate alleviates ovalbumin-induced allergic responses in Brown Norway rats: associations with immunoglobulin E-related responses and the gut microbiota-short-chain fatty acid axis.

studies.authors: Wang, Yi, Wang, Xinze, Chen, Liang, Zhang, Xinxue et al.
studies.abstract: Whey protein hydrolysate (WPH) has considerable potential as a functional food ingredient; however, its role in alleviating allergic responses and the underlying mechanisms remain insufficiently understood, particularly the potential role of gut microbiota and their metabolites. This study characterized the structural changes of WPH following enzymatic hydrolysis, evaluated its effects on allergic responses in an ovalbumin-induced allergic rat model, and investigated the associated changes in gut microbiota and short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) to explore their potential involvement in the antiallergic effects of WPH. Whey protein hydrolysate was prepared by two-step enzymatic hydrolysis. Compared with whey protein isolate (WPI), the amide I band shifted from 1651.85 to 1654.62 cm Whey protein hydrolysate alleviated allergic responses by attenuating systemic allergic responses, reducing mast-cell activation and allergic mediator release, and partially restoring gut microbial richness and diversity, supporting its potential as a functional food ingredient. © 2026 Society of Chemical Industry.

studies.abstract: 5-Fluorouracil (5-FU)-induced oral mucositis (OM) is associated with the fat-tissue-associated protein (FTO)/cytidine monophosphate kinase 2 (CMPK2)/NOD-like receptor protein 3 (NLRP3) inflammatory axis. A hamster OM model was established using 5-FU injections and mechanical irritation, with LR administered in drinking water. Macroscopic scoring, histopathology, serum ELISA, and tissue oxidative markers were assessed. Protein expression of FTO, CMPK2, NLRP3, apoptosis-associated speck-like protein containing a CARD (ASC), and pro-caspase-1 was analyzed by western blot. In hamsters, LR significantly reduced mucosal ulceration (injury score from 3.67 ± 0.52 to 2.50 ± 0.84, LR alleviates 5-FU-induced OM by inhibiting the FTO/CMPK2/NLRP3 inflammasome axis, reducing inflammation and oxidative stress. These findings are supported by both overexpression and knockdown experiments, as well as by human-relevant insights into LR-microbiome interactions.

studies.title: Development of a Mast-Cell Activation Test for Diagnosing Allergic Rhinitis.
studies.authors: Pan, Jianli, Gong, Ling, Xu, Jie, Luo, Shiqiong et al.
studies.abstract: Serum-specific IgE (sIgE) and skin prick testing (SPT) have limitations in diagnosing allergic rhinitis (AR). CD63, a mast cell activation biomarker reflecting degranulation extent, has unclear application in AR diagnosis. This study developed a functional mast cell activation test (MAT) for the in vitro diagnosis of AR by quantifying CD63 expression on LAD2 cells stimulated with patient serum and specific allergens. The assay was evaluated in 128 AR patients and 115 controls. The assay showed good reproducibility (CV = 8.26%). In the test cohort, AR patients had significantly higher CD63-positive rates than controls (5.21% ± 4.55% vs. 1.39% ± 1.79%, p < 0.001). ROC analysis yielded an AUC of 0.84, with 94.60% specificity and 77.10% accuracy at a 2.09% cutoff, which was confirmed in the validation cohort (specificity 90.24%, accuracy 80.51%). In the overall population, CD63 AUC (0.85) was higher than that for histamine (0.68) and total IgE (tIgE, 0.83). The CD63-positive rate correlated strongly with sIgE (r = 0.59, p < 0.001) and total IgE (r = 0.42, p < 0.001), whereas its correlation with histamine release was weaker (r = 0.35 vs. sIgE). These findings support MAT based on mast cell CD63 as a precise functional tool for AR diagnosis.

studies.title: CD63 aptamer-based electrochemical sensor assesses stored red blood cell-derived exosome burden associated with mast-cell-mediated transfusion-related acute lung injury.
studies.authors: Zheng, Ling, Su, Shan-Shan, Qin, Sai-Nan, Ren, Yimin et al.
studies.abstract: Transfusion-related acute lung injury (TRALI) remains a serious complication of transfusion, and blood component-derived exosomes have been proposed as candidate contributors to transfusion-related inflammatory dysregulation. Rapid and practical methods to assess exosome burden in stored red blood cell (RBC) units remain limited. Here, we developed a CD63 electrochemical aptamer-based (E-AB) sensor as a preliminary analytical platform to rapidly detect exosome-associated signals and investigated whether stored red-blood-cell-derived exosomes (EXs-RBC) contribute to mast-cell-associated inflammatory lung injury in TRALI-relevant models. Using the CD63 E-AB sensor, we assessed EXs-RBC signals in stored RBC units, isolated EXs-RBC for HMC-1 cell stimulation and mouse experiments, and evaluated their inflammatory effects. The CD63 E-AB readout decreased in a concentration-dependent manner with increasing exosome levels. EXs-RBC dose-dependently amplified inflammatory responses, and these effects were attenuated by pharmacologic mast-cell inhibition or mast-cell deficiency. In antibody-independent TRALI-relevant inflammatory lung injury models and a supportive antibody-mediated TRALI-like model, EXs-RBC exacerbated lung injury and were associated with activation of the mast-cell toll-like receptor 3 (TLR3)-mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) signaling. Collectively, these findings support the feasibility of using a CD63 E-AB sensor to assess exosome burden in stored RBC units and provide experimental evidence that EXs-RBC can amplify mast-cell-associated inflammatory lung injury in TRALI-relevant models, supporting further investigation of EXs-RBC burden as a candidate donor-side metric in transfusion safety research.
